text: Congenital cataract is mainly caused by genetic or environmental factors, such as gene mutation or infection with rubella virus during early pregnancy [ 1 ]. It usually presents at birth and can be diagnosed by routine examination or is noticed in connection with leukocoria or strabismus. Congenital cataract is the most prevalent treatable cause of blindness and visual impairment in children; worldwide, there are 20,000–40,000 children born with congenital cataract each year [ 2 , 3 ]. Therefore, appropriate, effective, and timely surgery in children with congenital cataract is highly desirable, because it can reduce the rate of blindness and improve vision in young populations.
source_label: The role of primary intraocular lens implantation in the risk of secondary glaucoma following congenital cataract surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis
